findings.title: Call to non-existent no-arg isConditionalPasskeysEnabled() breaks compilation
findings.body: UsernameForm.authenticate() calls `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled()` with no arguments, but the only definition of that method in the hierarchy is `UsernamePasswordForm.isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(UserModel user)`, which takes one argument. Neither AbstractUsernameFormAuthenticator nor UsernamePasswordForm declares a no-arg overload, so this file does not compile. The intended call was presumably `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`.

findings.title: Conditional passkeys no longer initialized on fresh login (user == null)
findings.body: In authenticate(), the `webauthnAuth.fillContextForm(context)` call was moved out of the else branch and is now guarded by `isConditionalPasskeysEnabled(context.getUser())`, which returns false when the user is null. Previously the form was filled exactly in the user == null case (fresh login with no user in context). As a result, on an initial login (no re-authentication), the WebAuthn conditional UI attributes (challenge, rpId, ENABLE_WEBAUTHN_CONDITIONAL_UI) are never set, so discoverable-key/passkey login on the first login page is broken. The same regression applies to challenge(context, error, field) at line 137: after a failed login attempt where the user was cleared from the context, the passkeys UI will no longer be rendered even though the old code explicitly re-filled it when `context.getUser() == null`.
